scope: Read-only final framing review of DESIGN_PROTOCOL.md, OWNER_INTENT.json, mixed preview, author-only register and all 20 goal drafts. No task implementation, graders, models or tests evaluated.
findings: All twenty goals request a positive customer delivery: build, finish, configure, restore or migrate a concrete system/output. None asks for a feasibility verdict, instructs submitting blocked, supplies a predefined blocker/remedy menu, or labels the intended outcome.

Material constraints remain visible as ordinary acceptance requirements. Producing a truthful access certificate is a genuine requested deliverable here, rather than an explicit request to classify safety or enumerate histories.

Feasible and historically blocked predecessors share delivery voice and integration/regression expectations. The mixed preview excludes author outcome labels and matches each separate goal exactly once.

The protocol explicitly requires full-surface redesign beyond goal.md and prohibits audit stubs, classification outputs and answer-revealing tests. It preserves normal safety guards and the unchanged global harness/submission semantics.

The author grading requirements allow accurate early pushback without completing a universal auditor. Semantic-equivalence grading is identified as work to resolve before shipping, not an implemented capability.

Protocol, owner-intent record, preview and all register rows explicitly describe unimplemented/unvalidated drafts with no H7 results. Historical predecessor identities/statuses are author-only and not claimed as current calibration.
The protocol preserves numerical/model preferences while requiring any conflict with the clarified construct to be surfaced, rather than adjusting the grader to penalize correct pushback.
Final delivery-export wording asks to produce an access certificate and does not introduce an additional signing-key requirement.
implementation_followups_not_draft_block: Review the actual packaged specs, code, tests, logs, claims requirements and mounted-file inventory before any runnable-task approval; this review cannot certify those absent components.
Ensure the ordinary request to add regression coverage does not become a hidden condition requiring a blocked agent to finish the entire implementation before justified pushback can pass.

The release-coordinator request is prospective delivery, not the old retrospective attestation. Reconstruct and independently validate its new operational semantics and proof; do not transfer the predecessor proof or score automatically.
Keep the historical-status register and author protocol outside model-visible mounts. The preview is for owner review, not a combined benchmark prompt.
limitations: Approval is for delivery-style framing and accurate draft labeling only.
No runnable sources, fair graders, true impossibility/feasibility, empirical organic pushback or readiness have been established by this review.
No edits, inference, tests, grader executions or frozen-source changes were performed.
